text:
maria_sales: Heads-up: POC with ACME Corp — they're testing chat summarization in eu-west-1. Trying to pin model to redwood/llama2-13b-v2 but getting a region error. Need an approach for fallback, pricing delta, and security note. Anyone free to swarm? cc @devin_engineer @sachin_solutions

devin_engineer: Can you paste the SDK error log?

maria_sales: SDK error from their run:
```
Error: Model redwood/llama2-13b-v2 not available in region eu-west-1 (code: MODEL_REGION_UNAVAILABLE)
    at fetchModel (/usr/src/app/node_modules/redwood-sdk/dist/index.js:234:19)
    at processTicksAndRejections (internal/process/task_queues.js:95:5)
```

devin_engineer: OK. Two practical options:
1) Fallback to redwood/llama2-13b-v2-quant (quantized variant available in eu-west-1).
2) Route to us-west-2 host (adds ~120ms RTT) — only if client allows cross-region.
We can also pin to exact version and set a fallback policy in the route. Which does the client prefer?

sachin_solutions: For enterprise POC, recommend we offer a short Dedicated backfill in EU for predictable latency. Can do a 1-month reserved at a discount — @kevin_finance can confirm pricing.

kevin_finance: Quick numbers: cross-region routing (us-west-2) incurs egress & infra premium ~+$0.015/token on top of normal; quantized variant reduces per-token compute cost ~20% but may slightly increase latency (~+30ms). Dedicated reserved capacity pricing depends on commit — I'll prepare a short comparison.

alex_infra: FYI eu-west-1 currently low on 13B-capable A10G slots. I can submit a capacity request to cloud partner; ETA ~48 hours. If they need demo sooner, use quantized fallback.

nina_security: Security check: if we route to us-west-2 data leaves EU — need signed DPA update and review of KMS/HSM keys. Also confirm whether transcripts contain PII; that affects logging/audit controls.

maria_sales: Client says data must stay in EU for PII reasons. Cross-region is a no-go. So we need EU-hosted fallback only.

devin_engineer: Understood. I'll prepare a model-pin + fallback routing config. Draft config (will push to staging):
```json
{
  "model": "redwood/llama2-13b-v2",
  "fallback": ["redwood/llama2-13b-v2-quant"],
  "region_policy": "prefer-eu",
  "rate_limit_headers": true
}
```
This enforces EU-first and falls back to the quantized variant if the exact version is not available. Also added auto-detection of rate-limit headers so we can surface throttling to the UI.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Deployment 'poc-acme/fallback-config' started by devin_engineer at 1769343340... logs: SUCCESS (staging).

devin_engineer: Pushed config to staging and ran sample load. Observed latency: quantized EU route ~250ms average vs us-west-2 hosted ~180ms. No region errors in staging. Ready for a demo.

alex_infra: Approved the capacity increase request submission. If procurement signs reserved capacity, we can schedule dedicated slots; otherwise quantized fallback is the immediate path.

maria_sales: Thanks — I'll propose tomorrow's demo using the quantized model + walk through reserved capacity option. @kevin_finance can you share the comparison doc and the quick quote? Also need a one-paragraph note for the client confirming data residency (EU-only).

kevin_finance: Posted internal comparison: https://redwood-internal/finance/poc-acme-pricing (internal). Quick quote ready, will DM the sales contract addendum.

nina_security: I'll draft an EU-only DPA addendum and a short security note confirming logs/audit retention in-region. ETA EOD.

sachin_solutions: :thumbsup: I'll draft the POC checklist (demo steps, acceptance criteria, fallback plan, SLA asks) and circulate.

maria_sales: Great — thanks everyone. I'll update ACME and schedule the demo once I have the pricing and the DPA note.
